title: Scholarship and Group Chat
premise: Gideon Lockridge transfers to Ashgrove Academy on a scholarship he can't afford to lose, only to discover the school's founding family built it atop a sealed well that grants answers to anyone who asks an honest question aloud. When a college essay prompt — 'What would you trade to be remembered?' — goes viral in the senior group chat, every answer becomes a binding wish, and the students start vanishing into the school's old stories. Gideon, whose own answer was a lie of desperation, must win the state championship and the hidden 'championship' beneath the school: a contest of truths against the well's keeper. In the end, Gideon sacrifices his scholarship and his recorded legacy to unseal the well, freeing his classmates but erasing himself from the yearbook — until Priya, the one friend who kept a paper copy of his essay, restores him by reading it aloud.
about_author: Lena Voss is a former debate coach who grew up in a mill town where the high school stood on land nobody would explain. She writes young adult fiction about institutions that keep secrets and the kids clever enough to survive them.

chapters.title: Day One of Four Hundred
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He arrives at Ashgrove counting down the 400 days to graduation, cataloguing exits and scholarship rules. A janitor warns him not to answer questions in the west hallway. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, the survival math of a poor kid among legacies.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the essay: 'What would you trade to be remembered?' The senior group chat erupts with jokes, then confessions. Gideon types a lie about wanting legacy; Priya notices his hesitation. Beat: the intoxicating danger of honesty in public.

chapters.title: West Hallway Rules
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He breaks the janitor's rule by answering a stranger's question aloud near the old well cover — 'What do you want most?' — and hears something answer back. That night his scholarship letter rewrites itself. Beat: dread mixed with terrible hope.

chapters.title: Group Chat Confessions
chapters.summary: Ensemble via chat logs and Marcus's POV. Students post real answers at midnight; by morning, three of them have uncanny luck. The chat becomes a ritual. Gideon stays silent, watching. Beat: complicity — everyone knows and no one says it.

chapters.title: Tryouts Don't Matter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He makes the quiz bowl team and the track relay, both meaningless to him compared to grades. Coach Reyes hints the school 'keeps its champions.' Priya asks what he traded. He lies again. Beat: the widening gap between performance and self.

chapters.title: The First Vanishing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Star swimmer Devon posts his true answer, wins everything, then stops existing in photos — but everyone remembers him wrong. Only the paper copies of essays hold the truth. Beat: grief for someone the world insists never happened.

chapters.title: Founders' Day Assembly
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Headmaster Lockridge — no relation, or so they say — celebrates the school's 150th year over the sealed well. Gideon finds his own surname in the founder's ledger as 'debtor.' Beat: inheritance as debt; the horror of belonging.

chapters.title: What Priya Asked
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She admits she asked the well how to be loved, and now she can't stop being agreeable — her opinions literally won't come out. Gideon promises to ask her question back for her. Beat: tenderness under coercion.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Terms
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the sub-basement he meets the Keeper, a student from 1899 who asked one honest question too many. Two championships exist: the visible season, and the truth-contest held each century. Losers are 'archived.' Beat: stakes made explicit; time already running out.

chapters.title: Midterms and Missing People
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Half the quiz bowl team is archived after a losing scrimmage. The administration files them as transfers. Parents don't call because parents forget. Beat: institutional gaslighting; rage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Reading the Essays Aloud
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The survivors read each other's original essays aloud, restoring fragments of the archived. Gideon refuses to let anyone read his — his essay contains the lie that anchors him to the well. Beat: intimacy as vulnerability; secrets as shields.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Quiz bowl regionals: Gideon carries the team while secretly using answers the well feeds him. They qualify for states. Winning feels like theft. Beat: hollow victory; the price of shortcuts compounding.

chapters.title: Lockridge Blood
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He confronts Headmaster Lockridge, who confesses the family founded the well to escape poverty — every generation pays a child to it. Gideon is this century's payment. Beat: betrayal by bloodline; fury and recognition.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks Her Silence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She forces her own words out — disagreeing publicly, cracking the agreeability curse — and discovers honest speech weakens the well. The group chat pivots from wishes to testimony. Beat: liberation; courage is contagious.

chapters.title: The Trade Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Keeper offers Gideon his dream: full ride, name on the founders' wall, everyone else archived. All he must do is lose the truth-contest on purpose. Beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable; despair's seduction.

chapters.title: States
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The state championship, played flawlessly and feeling irrelevant. Gideon throws the final match deliberately — sacrificing the scholarship path — because winning seals his contract. Beat: public failure as private salvation.

chapters.title: The Contest of Truths
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Beneath the school, Gideon faces the Keeper: each must speak a truth the other cannot bear. Gideon speaks his essay's lie aloud and then the truth behind it — that he'd trade anything to matter. The well begins to take him. Beat: climax; naked honesty as weapon and wound.

chapters.title: Archived
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Gideon vanishes; records erase him; even she feels his face blurring. But she kept his handwritten draft. The remaining students gather every copy of every essay ever written. Beat: darkest hour; memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Read Him Back
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the well's mouth, the survivors read Gideon's essay aloud — the lie and the correction — refusing to let the institution define him. The well, built on honest questions, cannot digest a truth told by someone else on your behalf. Beat: collective defiance; love as citation.

chapters.title: Unsealed
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He wakes in the sub-basement as the well cracks open, releasing a century of archived students as fading names spoken once more. The Keeper, finally answered honestly by someone, dissolves gratefully. Beat: release; grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Four Hundred Days, Recounted
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Scholarship gone, Gideon works nights and applies elsewhere; Priya edits his new essay — no trades, just truth. The school quietly fills the well shaft with concrete. Beat: quiet rebuilding; survival redefined as more than endurance.

chapters.title: What We Kept
chapters.summary: Ensemble, epilogue. Graduation day: the group chat renames itself 'The Archive' and posts one honest answer each, on paper, mailed to each other. Gideon reads his aloud, unafraid. Final beat: loyalty chosen over safety; truth as the only inheritance worth keeping.
